correctness.rationale: Each oriented Poisson caller splits into independent edge clocks, and the undirected contact rate is c=1/a+1/b. In state (i,j), transitions to (i+1,j) and (i,j+1) occur at rates (a−i)jc and (b−j)ic. A single B seed and a single A seed have first waits Exp(ac) and Exp(bc), then share the same independent (1,1) residual; strict stochastic dominance and mean gap (a−b)/(a+b) follow. For b,k fixed and a→∞, any initial B seed rapidly informs Θ(a^(2/3)) A vertices then all B in time a^(−1/3), while o(a) A vertices have been informed; residual max of a−o_P(a) independent Exp(1+b/a) gives standard Gumbel after log a. If all seeds are A, the independent initial first B-contact tends to Exp(k), and G+E_k follows; harmonic number means plus exp-small exceptional event bound give expectation limits. Fresh rational Markov recurrences independently confirmed 18 exact mean differences.

value.rationale: Fixed-width complete bicliques model an extreme but canonical hub/periphery graph. The source-location effect persists as an order-one entire limiting distribution, not just a leading log a term, and finite single-seed stochastic ordering holds at every deadline. This gives a precise mathematical explanation of why reaching the hub class matters more than adding a few peripheral seeds.
